look_here_first: GOOSEGRASS (INTRODUCED): go BASE → COLLAR → HEAD. (1) Annual fibrous-rooted rosette of very FLATTENED pale or silvery-white basal tillers; outward shoots come from one crown and do NOT form rooting stolons/rhizomes. (2) Young blades are FOLDED, not rolled; at the leaf-sheath junction examine a SHORT jagged, sometimes centrally notched MEMBRANOUS ligule (~0.2–1.5 mm depending on source), with hairs nearby but NOT a ligule made only of hairs. (3) A seedhead has several stiff FINGERLIKE branches, often one lower branch; each flat branch bears TWO neat zipperlike rows of flat AWNLESS spikelets. Mature spikelets about 3–7 mm and usually 3–9 fertile florets EACH; count florets inside ONE spikelet, not the seeds or branches. Only an original seedhead image was locally installed before this pass; new licensed Commons parts photographs are EXTERNAL references.

morphology_keys.life_cycle: Warm-season annual grass; fibrous-rooted tuft, not a creeping perennial rhizome/stolon network.
morphology_keys.habit: Flattened tillers radiate outward from a central, often whitish/silvery crown; stems may become ascending when unmowed. Mature plant is tough and often conspicuous in compacted turf or disturbed soil.
morphology_keys.leaves: Leaves are folded in the bud (vernation), with a pronounced keel/crease. Blade bases and collar may bear sparse long hairs; do not confuse those hairs with the ligule itself.
morphology_keys.collar_ligule: Short membranous ligule about 0.6–1.5 mm, often irregular/notched or split in the middle; auricles absent. Lift the blade away from its sheath and use a hand lens to see the membrane.
morphology_keys.flowering: Usually several (commonly 2–7, sometimes more) fingerlike, flattened racemes near the tip; the awnless, laterally compressed, multi-flowered spikelets are densely arranged in two ranks, like a zipper. An additional branch may be inserted slightly below the main cluster.
morphology_keys.roots_and_nodes: Fibrous roots at the central crown; spreading goosegrass tillers generally do not root at successive nodes, unlike stoloniferous Bermudagrass.
morphology_keys.habitat: Sunny, compacted and repeatedly trafficked lawns, paths, bed margins and other disturbed ground; tolerates close mowing.
best_field_traits: INTRODUCED, warm-season fibrous-rooted ANNUAL; goosegrass can tolerate traffic and very close mowing, and its flattened radiating tillers form a rosette.
THE BASE: pale/whitish, very conspicuously flattened compressed sheaths and stem bases radiating from ONE tough center; no long runner network rooting at successive nodes.
FOLDED young leaf (vernation), blade with prominent midvein; leaves generally smooth but longer sparse collar/blade-base hairs may occur.
LIGULE: short (~0.2–1.5 mm) jagged/notched MEMBRANOUS collar ligule, no auricles; side hairs are NOT a solely hair-fringed ligule (contrast Cynodon).

HEAD: often 2–10+ stout fingerlike flattened racemes, some may be just below terminal digitate group; individual spikes bear neat parallel two-rank arrays of closely appressed, generally AWNLESS spikelets.

ONE SPIKELET: compressed, usually about 3–7 mm depending on flora, typically 3–9 fertile FLORETS; distinguish a spikelet from the multi-spikelet flowering branch, count individual florets inside the one whole spikelet.

CRABGRASS: Digitaria has paired or otherwise arranged much smaller, typically two-floret-unit spikelets on finer racemes. Distinguish using the entire plant and one ripe spikelet, not only the radial seedhead.
BERMUDAGRASS: Cynodon is a rooted stolon/rhizome perennial with a short HAIR-FRINGE ligule and one fertile floret per spikelet (goosegrass annual no rooted runners, membrane ligule).
FEATHER FINGERGRASS: Chloris spp. can have fingerheads but awns and hairy floret tips look feathery instead of Eleusine's smooth dense zippers.
what_to_photograph_for_confirmation: ROOTED CROWN: whole pulled annual plant including fibrous roots and strongly flattened whitish tiller bases; small scale at the central pale crown; document absence of rooted runners.
FOLDED NEW BUD: expose newly emerging blade cross-section, compare same-scale crabgrass rolled vernation.
TRUE LIGULE 10–20×: open blade/sheath junction and point to jagged/notched ~0.2–1.5 mm transparent MEMBRANE, not adjacent collar hairs; include mm ruler.
ONE FLAT FLOWER BRANCH: side and face view demonstrating two tight rows of AWNLESS closely appressed spikelets and any lower-subtending flowering branch.
ONE FULL RIPE SPIKELET 10–20×: photograph two lower glumes plus ~3–9 fertile florets in a 3–7 mm compressed spikelet with 1-mm scale. Label florets INSIDE, not whole spikelets.
CONTROL LOOKALIKES: separately image Digitaria paired spikelet, Cynodon true rooted stolon and short hair-fringe ligule, and Chloris plumose long awns.

PUBLIC SAFE PHOTO: get an actual archived exact-species CC0/CC BY/CC BY-SA collar and crown JPG; existing CC BY-NC-SA original still carries explicit public photo-rights hold and must not be silently released.
crew_field_check: GOOSEGRASS (INTRODUCED): go BASE → COLLAR → HEAD. (1) Annual fibrous-rooted rosette of very FLATTENED pale or silvery-white basal tillers; outward shoots come from one crown and do NOT form rooting stolons/rhizomes. (2) Young blades are FOLDED, not rolled; at the leaf-sheath junction examine a SHORT jagged, sometimes centrally notched MEMBRANOUS ligule (~0.2–1.5 mm depending on source), with hairs nearby but NOT a ligule made only of hairs. (3) A seedhead has several stiff FINGERLIKE branches, often one lower branch; each flat branch bears TWO neat zipperlike rows of flat AWNLESS spikelets. Mature spikelets about 3–7 mm and usually 3–9 fertile florets EACH; count florets inside ONE spikelet, not the seeds or branches. Only an original seedhead image was locally installed before this pass; new licensed Commons parts photographs are EXTERNAL references.

CRABGRASS / Digitaria ciliaris: often digitate narrow head too, but spikelets are paired or arranged less rigidly along finer axes, each normally with a fertile upper and sterile lower floret; it lacks the characteristic chunky pale flattened goosegrass center. Many crabgrasses have a ROLLED young leaf where goosegrass has FOLDED vernation, but confirm the actual species before relying on this. BERMUDAGRASS / Cynodon dactylon: a PERENNIAL with true soil-running stolons that root at nodes and underground rhizomes; very short HAIR-FRINGED ligule; one-floret spikelets rather than the many-floreted goosegrass spikelet. FEATHER FINGERGRASS / Chloris virgata: fingers look hairy/FEATHERY from conspicuously LONG awns and lemma-tip hairs; goosegrass spikes are smooth-coarse and awnless in tidy flat two-row zipper units. CROWFOOTGRASS / Dactyloctenium aegyptium: compact broad spike-fingers are often short or claw-shaped, sometimes with projected point on the end; use spikelet glume/awn key. Do NOT judge from a top-down crown-like seedhead image alone.

Have a crew member compare 3 real parts on ONE fresh plant (white compressed crown, rolled/folded new bud, true ligule), then examine one mature spikelet under 10–20×. Source-author photo annotations are on the Commons spikelet panel: do not add speculative arrows.

confused_with: Digitaria ciliaris (southern crabgrass) and other Digitaria spp.

key_distinctions.look_here_first: Inspect the central crown and a NEW folded/rolled leaf, then compare flowering branches.
key_distinctions.goosegrass: Strongly flattened pale basal tillers, folded young blades and coarse two-ranked zipperlike branches.
key_distinctions.lookalike: Crabgrasses typically have rolled young blades, more slender racemes, and a less distinctly flattened silvery crown; verify Digitaria species separately.
key_distinctions.caution: Both can have fingerlike seedheads; a single top-down seedhead photograph is not enough.

key_distinctions.look_here_first: Follow a low shoot across the soil to see whether it roots at nodes; inspect ligule with a hand lens.
key_distinctions.goosegrass: Annual tuft with flattened white crown, no spreading rooted stolon/rhizome network, short MEMBRANOUS ligule.
key_distinctions.lookalike: Bermudagrass is a perennial that spreads through rooted aboveground stolons and underground rhizomes; its ligule is a very short FRINGE of hairs.
key_distinctions.caution: Both may have radiating fingerlike flower branches; do not rely on branch number alone.

key_distinctions.look_here_first: Magnify an individual spikelet and check for long awns.
key_distinctions.goosegrass: Broad, overlapping, AWNLESS multi-flowered spikelets packed like a zipper on each branch.
key_distinctions.lookalike: Feather fingergrass has conspicuously awned, hairy spikelets that make its fingerlike branches appear feathery rather than smooth and zipperlike.
key_distinctions.caution: Awn characters require a focused close-up; a distant inflorescence silhouette is insufficient.

field_matrix.where_to_look: Whole flattened center + fresh folded or rolled bud + one mature spikelet
field_matrix.goosegrass: Compressed silver-white annual center and folded young leaf; one 3–7 mm spikelet generally has 3–9 florets
field_matrix.look_alike: Often more delicate head with paired small spikelets each with lower sterile and upper fertile floret; new bud often rolled
field_matrix.quick_rule: Don't infer genus from fingerhead silhouette. Count florets in a real spikelet.

field_matrix.where_to_look: Follow actual horizontal creeping stem, its rooting nodes and ligule
field_matrix.goosegrass: Annual from tough compressed tuft; short MEMBRANE ligule; no perennial rooted stolon/rhizome network
field_matrix.look_alike: Perennial with aboveground runners rooting at nodes and underground rhizomes; very short hair-fringe ligule
field_matrix.quick_rule: Rooted runner + hair ligule = Cynodon rather than Eleusine.

field_matrix.where_to_look: One fertile spikelet and awn tip under hand lens
field_matrix.goosegrass: Stout flat neat 2-row spikelets with 3–9 florets and no awns
field_matrix.look_alike: Awned and hairy seedheads create feathery bristly outlines
field_matrix.quick_rule: Branched feathery awns vs smooth zipper spikelets.

field_matrix.where_to_look: Tips of each short clawlike flowering branch, glume/awn and actual spikelet
field_matrix.goosegrass: Elongated flattened radiating spikes with dense 2-ranked awnless spikelets
field_matrix.look_alike: Often short thick crowfoot spikes ending in a bristly point; glumes may be awned
field_matrix.quick_rule: Fingerhead shape alone is shared; examine one branch tip and glume.

photo_diagnostic_lesson.title: Goosegrass — pale annual crown → true collar → zipper-row flowering head → multiflowered spikelet

steps.look: Flattened pale crown, fibrous roots, no rooting runners
steps.text: Compare the existing Bob Harms dry rooted whole-plant photograph (teaching panel 10) with the flowering tuft in habitat (panel 1). The actual fibrous root system is photographed, but neither image verifies a fresh living whitish compressed basal rosette continuously attached to the same flowering head. For a new field photo, lift a Hays-vouchered plant and photograph the living pale crown, folded emerging leaf, roots and attached culm with a centimeter ruler. Do not call the separate bermudagrass stolon comparison a goosegrass runner.
steps.photo_status: ROOTS AND FLOWERING HABIT PHOTOGRAPHED; LIVING CONNECTED PALE CROWN MACRO MISSING

steps.look: Short membranous ligule with nearby longer hairs
steps.text: Existing actual Eleusine collar photographs (panels 2 and 4) show the blade–sheath junction and nearby hairs; two gross arrows in panel 2 point to the junction and distinct side hairs, not to a measured free ligule edge. Published short membranous ligule approximately 0.2–1.5 mm varies by treatment. Open the inner collar on the same vouchered plant at 10–20× beside a real 1-mm ruler before marking its free edge or reporting its length. Unlike Cynodon, do not identify goosegrass by a hair-fringe-only ligule.
steps.photo_status: REAL COLLAR PHOTOGRAPHS AND GROSS ARROWS PRESENT; MEMBRANE LENGTH UNMEASURED

steps.look: Several stout fingers with two zipperlike rows of flattened, awnless spikelets
steps.text: Existing Bob Harms panels 9 and 8 show a complete attached head and the flat two-ranked spikelet arrangement; the original flowering photo is panel 0. This gross architecture is photographed and does not need another generic seedhead. Compare with Digitaria (panel 11), bermudagrass rooted stolon (panel 12), and Chloris awned spikelets (panel 13); check the base and ligule as well as the head.
steps.photo_status: ATTACHED HEAD AND TWO-RANKED SPIKELETS PHOTOGRAPHED; LOCAL MATCHED LOOK-ALIKE QA PENDING

steps.look: One flattened 3–7 mm spikelet, usually 3–9 florets, two short glumes and awnless fertile lemmas
steps.text: The photographer-annotated Harry Rose spikelet (panel 3) already labels true glumes and separate lemma/palea units; Bob Harms panels 5–6 provide additional genuine reproductive views. These source images are not a calibrated 1-mm dissection. Published comparative ranges (not measured from photos): lower glume about 1.5–2.5 mm, upper glume about 2–4.5 mm, and fertile lemma about 2.5–5 mm. Photograph one mature vouchered spikelet at 10–20× with separated glumes, at least three identifiable florets and a physical 1-mm bar. Never count finger branches as florets or claim individual microscopic arrow targets not visible in pixels.
steps.photo_status: SOURCE-LABELLED SPIKELET ANATOMY PRESENT; CALIBRATED DISSECTION AND ORGAN MEASUREMENTS MISSING

field_id_finish_pass.status_note: Existing photo inspected; two arrow pointers verified for radiating racemes and closely attached spikelets. True collar, silvery crown, individual fertile florets NOT resolved by this photo.
field_id_finish_pass.crew_teaching_summary: GOOSEGRASS (INTRODUCED): go BASE → COLLAR → HEAD. (1) Annual fibrous-rooted rosette of very FLATTENED pale or silvery-white basal tillers; outward shoots come from one crown and do NOT form rooting stolons/rhizomes. (2) Young blades are FOLDED, not rolled; at the leaf-sheath junction examine a SHORT jagged, sometimes centrally notched MEMBRANOUS ligule (~0.2–1.5 mm depending on source), with hairs nearby but NOT a ligule made only of hairs. (3) A seedhead has several stiff FINGERLIKE branches, often one lower branch; each flat branch bears TWO neat zipperlike rows of flat AWNLESS spikelets. Mature spikelets about 3–7 mm and usually 3–9 fertile florets EACH; count florets inside ONE spikelet, not the seeds or branches. Only an original seedhead image was locally installed before this pass; new licensed Commons parts photographs are EXTERNAL references.
lookalike_comparison: CRABGRASS / Digitaria ciliaris: often digitate narrow head too, but spikelets are paired or arranged less rigidly along finer axes, each normally with a fertile upper and sterile lower floret; it lacks the characteristic chunky pale flattened goosegrass center. Many crabgrasses have a ROLLED young leaf where goosegrass has FOLDED vernation, but confirm the actual species before relying on this. BERMUDAGRASS / Cynodon dactylon: a PERENNIAL with true soil-running stolons that root at nodes and underground rhizomes; very short HAIR-FRINGED ligule; one-floret spikelets rather than the many-floreted goosegrass spikelet. FEATHER FINGERGRASS / Chloris virgata: fingers look hairy/FEATHERY from conspicuously LONG awns and lemma-tip hairs; goosegrass spikes are smooth-coarse and awnless in tidy flat two-row zipper units. CROWFOOTGRASS / Dactyloctenium aegyptium: compact broad spike-fingers are often short or claw-shaped, sometimes with projected point on the end; use spikelet glume/awn key. Do NOT judge from a top-down crown-like seedhead image alone.
photo_targets: ROOTED CROWN: whole pulled annual plant including fibrous roots and strongly flattened whitish tiller bases; small scale at the central pale crown; document absence of rooted runners.
FOLDED NEW BUD: expose newly emerging blade cross-section, compare same-scale crabgrass rolled vernation.
TRUE LIGULE 10–20×: open blade/sheath junction and point to jagged/notched ~0.2–1.5 mm transparent MEMBRANE, not adjacent collar hairs; include mm ruler.
ONE FLAT FLOWER BRANCH: side and face view demonstrating two tight rows of AWNLESS closely appressed spikelets and any lower-subtending flowering branch.
ONE FULL RIPE SPIKELET 10–20×: photograph two lower glumes plus ~3–9 fertile florets in a 3–7 mm compressed spikelet with 1-mm scale. Label florets INSIDE, not whole spikelets.
CONTROL LOOKALIKES: separately image Digitaria paired spikelet, Cynodon true rooted stolon and short hair-fringe ligule, and Chloris plumose long awns.

PUBLIC SAFE PHOTO: get an actual archived exact-species CC0/CC BY/CC BY-SA collar and crown JPG; existing CC BY-NC-SA original still carries explicit public photo-rights hold and must not be silently released.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 01 · PALE FLATTENED ANNUAL CROWN
field_id_short_tiles.short: LOOK HERE FIRST: pale compressed tiller bases radiating from one tough fibrous-rooted center
field_id_short_tiles.details: Bob Harms's source-identified dried uprooted specimen (panel 10) shows true fibrous roots and attached flattened culms, while Harry Rose's in-situ photo (panel 1) shows field growth but hides the root crown. Goosegrass is an annual bunchgrass with notably compressed pale/whitish basal sheaths in life, NOT a network of rooting perennial runners. Neither photograph proves the LIVE milky-white crown at diagnostic close range. Next photograph: fresh uprooted living crown, fibrous roots, emerging tillers and cm scale.
field_id_short_tiles.status: DRIED ROOTED WHOLE PLANT AND IN-SITU HABIT PHOTO; PALE LIVING CROWN MACRO STILL NEEDED

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 02 · SHORT NOTCHED MEMBRANOUS LIGULE
field_id_short_tiles.short: Open the blade–sheath junction: ~0.3–1 mm short membrane, sometimes ciliate or split
field_id_short_tiles.details: Look at Harry Rose's independently CC BY 2.0 licensed photographed INNER blade–sheath junction (panel 2): it shows a pale joining rim and longer side hairs. Bob Harms's photograph (panel 4) adds another actual collar-area view. Penn State describes a small centrally divided jagged MEMBRANOUS ligule typically 1–1.5 mm; Harry Rose describes ~0.5–1 mm. No existing photo provides a physical millimeter ruler for the free membrane. The two arrows identify the collar search region and separate lateral hairs only, NOT certified membrane length.
field_id_short_tiles.status: TRUE COLLAR PHOTO PLUS TWO GROSS ARROWS; MEMBRANE EDGE NOT CALIBRATED

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 03 · TWO ZIPPER ROWS ON FLAT FINGERS
field_id_short_tiles.short: Several stiff digitate or subdigitate branches carry two neat ranks of tightly appressed spikelets
field_id_short_tiles.details: Bob Harms's actual complete attached head (panel 9) and raceme macro (panel 8) show the stout fingerlike branches with neatly paired ranks of nearly awnless flattened spikelets; the original NC-SA flowering photo is panel 0 and remains license-conditional. Head architecture is photographed, but not continuously linked to one locally collected living crown. An additional head-only picture is not a priority.
field_id_short_tiles.status: COMPLETE ATTACHED FLOWERING HEAD AND ZIPPER ROWS PHOTOGRAPHED

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 04 · MULTIFLORED 4–7 MM SPIKELET
field_id_short_tiles.short: One flattened spikelet contains about 3–9 florets, not just one or two
field_id_short_tiles.details: Harry Rose's real, source-PREANNOTATED multi-flowered spikelet (panel 3) identifies lower and upper GLUMES plus at least two separately labelled LEMMA/PALEA pairs; Bob Harms's source macro (panel 5) provides another reproductive view. Flora descriptions give roughly 3–9 florets per flattened spikelet, but these particular pictures lack physical mm scales. A single spikelet is NOT the full fingerlike branch. Distinguish author annotations from a new validated calibrated dissection.
field_id_short_tiles.status: REAL SOURCE-ANNOTATED GLUMES/LEMMAS VISIBLE; 1-MM VOUCHER DISSECTION MISSING

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 05 · TWO SHORT GLUMES, AWNLESS LEMMAS
field_id_short_tiles.short: Lower glume ~1.5–2.5 mm; upper ~2–4.5 mm; fertile lemmas ~2.5–5 mm (NZ flora)
field_id_short_tiles.details: Photographed actual source labels on panel 3 show two glumes, lemmas and paleas; see panel 5 for reproductive context. Goosegrass fertile lemmas are generally awnless and keeled, with multiple florets in one spikelet. Never claim lengths or count invisible units directly from these photographs; a ruler and separated mature floret series remain necessary for certification.
field_id_short_tiles.status: REAL SOURCE-ANNOTATED GLUMES/LEMMAS VISIBLE; LENGTHS NOT PHOTO-MEASURED

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 06 · CHECK CRABGRASS, BERMUDA AND CHLORIS
field_id_short_tiles.short: Count florets, inspect the ligule and follow runners before deciding from a fingerhead
field_id_short_tiles.details: Compare actual OTHER-species panel 11 (Digitaria ciliaris), panel 12 (Cynodon dactylon stolon), and panel 13 (Chloris virgata feathery awned head) with goosegrass panel 2 (short membranous collar). Bermudagrass roots at runner nodes and has a hair-fringe ligule; Chloris can have long bristly awns; Digitaria differs in small/floret arrangement. Identify by BASE + COLLAR + SPIKELET together, not a fingerhead alone.
field_id_short_tiles.status: FIELD COMPARISON — MATCHED LOCAL SPECIMENS/PHOTO QA PENDING
